knowledge.details: The system successfully identified all 13 major contacts from ground truth with correct names, emails, companies, and titles. However, it misclassified Pierre Durand's relationship type (direct_report vs colleague), and had inconsistent tone classifications (using 'professional' instead of 'casual'/'semi-formal'). Interaction counts are inflated across most contacts (e.g., Pierre: 27 vs 20, Camille: 11 vs 6). The system added 12 additional contacts (team emails, automated systems, newsletters) not in ground truth - while some may be valid, they dilute precision. Projects are well-captured with 5/5 matched, though naming differs slightly (e.g., 'Partenariat GlobalTech' vs 'GlobalTech Partnership'). Terminology section is good with 10/10 terms captured plus 2 additional valid terms. Topics are generally accurate but sometimes more verbose than ground truth. The addition of 'frequent_topics' array is useful. Overall, the output would be helpful for email drafting but needs refinement on relationship types, tone consistency, and interaction count accuracy.

rules.details:
COMPLETENESS: System found 10/13 ground truth contacts (77%), missing john.smith@globaltech.com and adding 3 hallucinated contacts (equipe-digitale, recrutement, it-support). Found 12/12 general rules conceptually but with different categorizations. Missing 2 auto_reply_patterns entirely (0/2). Overall ~65% complete.

PRECISION: Major tone mismatches hurt precision significantly. Pierre marked 'semi-formal' vs 'casual' in GT. Nicolas marked 'formal' vs 'semi-formal'. prospect-startup marked 'formal' vs 'semi-formal'. Claire marked 'formal' vs 'semi-formal'. CEO marked 'formal' vs 'semi-formal'. These tone errors would produce wrong formality levels in generated emails. Greeting variations are acceptable but tone errors affect email quality. Rules are conceptually sound but over-segmented (e.g., vouvoiement split into 3 rules vs 1 in GT). Signatures hardcoded in contact rules rather than handled dynamically via general rules. ~55% precision due to tone errors and structural issues.

USEFULNESS: Would produce mostly functional drafts but with wrong formality level for 5 key contacts: Pierre (too formal - critical for daily team communication), Nicolas (too formal), prospect-startup (too formal), Claire (too formal), and CEO (too formal). Missing auto-reply patterns reduces automation value. Over-detailed contact rules with hardcoded signatures reduce maintainability and flexibility. Language detection works correctly. Greeting/closing patterns mostly correct. ~60% useful - functional baseline but needs correction for key contacts to be production-ready.
